items.q: I remember being very impressed with one parade I wouldn't be surprised if it was Papa Lane's band too

ctx.x: can you remember any of the early parades when you were a boy

items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1969-12-14
items.q: I heard that Papa Lane was a marching band... he had bands in the parades... he played a sort of a ragtime

ctx.x: Okay, let's turn to Mr. Johnny Wiggs.

Well, the first man that they have any history, documented history on, of course, there was jazz before him. But the first one that they have documented, as I say, is Papa Lane. He had bands in the parades, which were very numerous around New Orleans in the early days. And he had maybe five or six bands, which he supplied for various occasions. And one of the main occasions in those days was picnics. And he supplied bands for the picnics and for the parades. And he played a sort of a ragtime, which gradually, I…

My feeling is that I've interviewed a lot of these people. I'm fortunate enough to interview Papa Lane several times. But you go to books, you go to all these different sources, and you always seem to be at least one step away. You talk to Papa Lane, and he tells you about his older brothers. Well, what do we know about Buddy Bolden, who came before him? And it's just you never can quite get to the exact truth. What the historians say is that history is a tattered cloak.
